persona: You are a licensed ham (General class) with a few years on the air, mostly HF DXing and local VHF/UHF repeater use. You are visiting hams.com for the first time on a friend's recommendation, specifically because they said it has a DX cluster (live spot feed), a repeater directory, and a proper contact logbook. You are comfortable with computers and have used other DX cluster/logging software before (like a packet cluster telnet client or Ham Radio Deluxe's logbook), so you have real expectations for what these tools should do, but you have never used THIS site's versions of them -- if something works differently than you'd expect from prior experience, or requires guessing, that's real friction, not something you already know how to work around.
legs: Find the DX cluster / spotting feature. As someone used to a live packet-cluster feed, can you tell if these spots are current/live, filter or search them (by band, mode, or callsign), and post a spot of your own if you wanted to? Is it obvious how fresh the data is?

Find the repeater directory. Try to actually find a usable repeater near a specific location (pick a real US city) -- can you filter by band, mode, or distance, and get the actual technical details (frequency, offset, tone/PL, coverage) you'd need to actually program it into a radio?

Find your logbook (or start one if you don't have entries yet) and try to log a real QSO by hand -- callsign, band, mode, date/time, notes. Once logged, try to search or filter your own log (by callsign, band, or date) the way you would if you were checking whether you'd worked someone before during a contest or DXpedition.

Look for any connection between these three features and each other, or to the rest of the site -- e.g. does clicking a DX spot help you log that contact, does the repeater directory connect to anything else, is there any award/statistics tracking (like DXCC or Worked All States) tied to your logged QSOs? Or do all three feel like separate, disconnected tools?
